overview.description: Traversone, also known as Ciapano, Rovescino, Tressette a non Prendere, Perdivinci, or Vinciperdi, is an Italian reverse Tressette trick-taking game. Players follow Tressette play but try to avoid taking point cards; the player who accumulates the penalty total loses unless a successful cappotto reverses the result.

history.origins: Traversone, also called Ciapano and Rovescino, is the reverse game of Tressette. It is a Lombardy and central Italian trick-taking game whose objective is to avoid taking point cards.
timeline: 20th century: Ciapano/Traversone documented as a reverse Tressette game in Italy.
history.evolution: Busca and Mattazza are variants of the Ciapano/Traversone reverse Tressette family.
history.cultural: Ciapano was very popular in Lombardy until the 1980s and is still played there.

setup.deck: 40-card Italian deck. Rank high to low follows Tressette: 3, 2, Ace, King, Knight, Jack, 7, 6, 5, 4.
setup.dealing: Deal all possible cards equally, anticlockwise; with four players each receives 10 cards.

rules.objective: Avoid taking point cards. A player who reaches the agreed penalty total loses, unless taking all points by cappotto reverses the penalty.
rules.gameplay: Players must follow suit if possible. There are no trumps; the highest card of the led suit wins the trick and leads next. Card points are counted as penalties instead of rewards.
keyRules: Uses Tressette ranking and no trump suit.
Point cards captured in tricks are bad.
A player who captures all available points makes cappotto and can reverse the penalty according to table rules.

strategy.basic: Avoid Aces (they're worth the most penalty). Dump high cards on others' leads.
strategy.intermediate: Deliberately go for Cappotto if you have overwhelming strength (reverses penalty to opponents).
strategy.advanced: Count points taken. Decide when to attempt Cappotto vs play safe.
tips: The last trick is worth 1 penalty point.
Cappotto is a high-risk, high-reward move.

list.name: Busca
list.description: Four-player variant in which players must take at least one point but avoid taking the most points; the Ace of Coins is a special high-value card.

list.name: Mattazza
list.description: Four-player variant in which both the highest and lowest point totals can be punished, making the middle score safest.

engine.deckDescription: A stripped French deck containing 40 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and eight ranks per suit (6 through Ace), created by removing all 2s through 5s from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy recognition during gameplay.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit in ascending order: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank determines card strength and eligibility for building sequences.
